title: OER repository submission channel + acceptance flow
context: Repository submission is the 'self-serve fallback' adoption channel: if no pilot teacher is secured, publishing to an OER repository at least makes plans discoverable and reusable, though it is explicitly 'publication, not adoption.' But even as a fallback, repository submission requires research: each repository has different submission requirements, metadata formats, license acceptance criteria, and review processes. Without a documented, working submission channel, plans cannot reach repository partners. This task researches the submission flow for at least one OER repository and establishes a repeatable, documented process for all future plan submissions.
objective: Research and document a working OER repository submission channel: submission requirements, metadata format, license acceptance criteria, review process, and how to record acceptance evidence for the outcome ledger.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one OER repository submission channel is researched and documented: submission URL, required metadata fields, accepted license types, review/acceptance process, and typical turnaround time.
The submission process for the repository is tested with at least one pilot plan: a plan is submitted and the outcome (accepted, pending, rejected with reason) is recorded.
Acceptance evidence format is defined: what constitutes verified acceptance (a live URL, an acceptance email, a repository record) and how to record it in the outcome ledger.
The document covers how LRMI/schema.org metadata (from task-011) and CC packages (from task-016) map to the repository's required format.
The documented process is repeatable: a future contributor can follow the steps without additional research to submit subsequent plans.
No account credentials or API tokens are committed; submission is either manual or uses a public-access flow.
resources: teacher-lesson-plans-partner-013 — confirmed partner (may include a repository partner)
OER Commons — https://www.oercommons.org/ (submission process research target)
PLAN.md — §Sustainability & maintenance (outcome tracking and repository fallback)
output: A committed document describing a working OER repository submission channel: requirements, metadata mapping, tested submission process, acceptance evidence format, and instructions for repeatable future submissions.
